title: Spare Capacity Playbook — QA Scenarios (July 2025)
content:
Overview:

Purpose: quick, operational playbook and worked examples for sizing and using spare GPU capacity across regions. This is intended for on-call SREs, infra planners, and product ops during capacity crunches and scheduled maintenance windows.

Scope: multi-region inference fleet (hosted + dedicated pools). Focused on spare capacity sizing, emergency failover steps, traffic rebalancing orders, and a rotation policy for DR reserves. Not a procurement plan — assumes spare capacity is available as soft reserve or burstable nodes.

Glossary (short):
- spare pool: GPUs reserved for unexpected demand or DR failover; not used for steady-state allocations
- reserve margin: target % headroom above predicted peak to keep in spare pool
- warm-standby: pre-initialized instances with model weights loaded but no active traffic
- cold-burst: nodes that require model load (~5–12 min) before serving
- drain: stop routing new requests to a node and let in-flight finish

Assumptions (current baseline):
- global q2-2025 peak demand: 7,600 concurrent generation tokens-per-second (approx) spread across 6 regions
- average model footprint (A100-80GB equivalent) per replica: ~1 unit (normalized)
- production SLO: p95 inference latency < 250ms (regional)
- target utilization band for serving nodes: 40–70% (above 70% increases tail latency risk)

Sizing methodology (summary):
1) Derive regional peak demand (historical 95th percentile over trailing 30d).
2) Compute baseline replicas = ceil(peak_demand / replica_capacity). We use replica_capacity = 120 concurrent gen tokens/s per normalized replica for mixed sequence workloads.
3) Spare reserve = max( hard_min, ceil(baseline_replicas * reserve_pct) ) subject to region max_pool caps.
   - recommended reserve_pct: 20% for primary regions, 30% for small or high-risk regions (e.g., APAC with single provider).
   - hard_min: 2 replicas for small regions, 8 for core regions (us-west/us-east).
4) DR buffer: additional replicas kept across two secondary regions to cover full-region loss for top-2 traffic regions (see rotation policy).

Worked example (us-west):
- 30d 95th peak: 1800 tokens/s
- replica_capacity: 120 tokens/s
- baseline_replicas = ceil(1800 / 120) = 15 replicas
- reserve_pct = 20% => spare_replicas = ceil(15 * 0.2) = 3 replicas
- apply hard_min (8) for core region => final spare_pool = max(3, 8) = 8 replicas
- operational available serving replicas = 15 baseline + 8 spare = 23 replicas; target utilization = 1800 / (23*120) = 65%

Region profile snapshot (text table):
Region | 30d95_peak | baseline_repl | spare_pct | spare_repl | hard_min | final_spare | notes
US-WEST | 1800 | 15 | 20% | 3 | 8 | 8 | core region, multi-AZ
US-EAST | 2200 | 19 | 20% | 4 | 8 | 8 | primary traffic hub
EU-CENTRAL | 1200 | 10 | 20% | 2 | 2 | 2 | limited burst capacity from partner
APAC-SG | 700 | 6 | 30% | 2 | 2 | 2 | single provider; higher reserve pct
SA-CENTRAL | 200 | 2 | 30% | 1 | 2 | 2 | low usage; keep minimal reserve

Failover mechanics (operational):
- Detection: Automated alarm triggers when region availability < 95% or node drain/oom rate > 3% sustained for 5m (Pager duty).
- Primary action: attempt intra-region scale-up (burstable soft reserve) until spare_pool exhausted. If still under SLO, proceed to cross-region spill.
- Cross-region spill order: nearest latency-compatible region(s) by routing policy (usually US-WEST -> US-EAST -> EU-CENTRAL). Use locality-pref fallback for reduced latency workloads.
- Model variant fallback: non-quantized heavy config -> quantized variant if available in the failover region to preserve throughput. Ensure model-variant compatibility list is current in ModelCatalog.

Traffic rebalancing steps (playbook):
1) Notify on-call: brief incident note with estimated deficit and likely spill regions.
2) Assess spare_pool remaining in primary region. If spare_pool >= required, scale and shift traffic locally; update console routing.
3) If insufficient, enable pre-approved cross-region fallback policy (route X% of traffic to target region). Start at low % (10–20%) and ramp 10% every 2 mins while monitoring p95 latency and error rate.
4) If latency or errors spike > 20% from baseline, pause ramp and consider model-variant fallback or reduce concurrency limit per-request.
5) When primary region healthy, drain cross-region nodes: reduce inbound traffic by 25% every 3 mins to avoid cold-start spikes.

DR Reserve Rotation Policy (quarterly rotate):
- Goal: keep DR pools warm and exercised to prevent bit-rot and allocation anti-patterns.
- Quarterly schedule: choose two candidate regions from the 3rd and 4th rank traffic buckets; exercise reserve by running controlled canary workloads for 24–48 hours.
- Validation checklist during exercise: weight hitting p95 latency < 250ms, model download times < 180s, KV-cache warm-up < 5% error on first 500 requests.
- Post-exercise: run a lightweight synthetic benchmark and commit results to Confluence (CONFT-4821) and mark the pool "validated".

Cost vs. Resilience tradeoffs (short):
- Keeping a large regional spare increases monthly GPU burn but reduces failover risk and customer-facing degradation. Use traffic-weighted risk scoring to justify increased reserves in high-ARR regions.
- Consider multi-tenant warm pools (shared between compatible customers) to amortize cost but ensure tenancy isolation boundaries and billing clarity.

Monitoring & Alerts (key thresholds):
- Region capacity_utilization_p95 > 72% -> warn (Slack #infra-alerts)
- Region capacity_utilization_p95 > 85% -> page on-call
- Sustained error-rate > 2.5% for 3m -> page and trigger failover checklist
- Cold-start_time_95p > 420s -> investigate AMI and model artifact availability

Simulation summary (recent dry-run 2025-06-20):
- Scenario: sudden 30% spike in US-EAST for 7m caused by experiment traffic mislabeling.
- Result: local spare absorbed 12% of spike; automated cross-region spill to US-WEST ramped to 40% over 6 mins and kept p95 within 240ms.
- Lessons: ramp steps at 2-min granularities slower than recommended; increased to 10%/2min in this playbook.

Operational runbook (quick steps):
- On-page: /infra/ops/runbook -> open incident play and assign one infra lead and one model ops lead.
- Immediate command snippets: (examples)
  - show region utilization: rcli region metrics us-west --window=5m
  - scale spare pool: rcli region reserve scale us-west --add 4
  - enable cross-region spill: rcli routing set-fallback --from us-east --to us-west --pct 20

Action items (owners):
- Update ModelCatalog compatibility matrix for all quantized variants (Claire Zhang) — due 2025-09-10
- Add automated DR exercise job to infra-schedule (Miguel Torres) — due 2025-08-01
- Reassess hard_min thresholds post-Q3 telemetry (Aisha Patel) — due 2025-10-01

Appendix — quick math reference:
- replica_capacity = historical concurrent tokens/s per replica (measure with synthetic mixed sequences)
- baseline = ceil(peak / replica_capacity)
- spare_replicas = max(hard_min, ceil(baseline * reserve_pct))
- end-state_util = peak / ((baseline + spare_replicas) * replica_capacity)

Notes / unresolved questions:
- Do we want to enable autoscaling of warm pools across regions automatically, or keep manual hops for billing control? (ops / finance decision)
- Need clearer mapping of customer-specific SLAs to regional DR priorities.
